declared_cases.note: Serious = at least one section carries a maximum sentence of 5+ years. Case 7 (Cr No 123/2018, Law & Order PS Bhimunipatnam; CC No 352/2018, 15th Metropolitan Magistrate) includes IPC 420 (cheating), which carries a maximum of 7 years and qualifies as serious; it shows 'Charges Framed: Yes' (16 Dec 2019) but no conviction. Case 3 also cites IPC 198 (using a false certificate as genuine), whose maximum sentence depends on the underlying proceeding and was not counted toward 'serious' given that ambiguity. The remaining cases involve IPC 143/149/188/149/290/341, CrPC 151, or Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, all capped at 2 years or less. Zero convictions.
